title: Utilizing primary HLA-G+ extravillous trophoblasts and HLA-G+ EVT-like cell lines to study maternal-fetal interactions
protocol: Remove the amnion by placing the placenta with the fetal surface facing upwards.
Peel off the amnion from the chorion towards the umbilical cord.
Drape the chorio-decidual membrane on palm with decidual surface facing upwards.
Gently separate decidua parietalis from chorion.
Cut 2 × 1 cm² thin sections of decidua basalis carefully from the maternal side of the placenta.
Collect approximately 15–20 pieces of decidua basalis.
Lay decidua basalis on finger with villi facing upwards.
Carefully remove villi from decidua basalis using scissors, avoiding buttonholing the tissue.
Gently scrape the chorion from the maternal decidua parietalis using sterile curved tip forceps.
Avoid necrotic or thickened, inflamed tissue and blood clots during scraping.
Do not allow chorionic membranes to dry out at any time.
Collect approximately 30 mL of chorionic membrane tissue in a labeled 50 mL conical tube containing 20 mL wash medium A.
Collect decidua parietalis tissue in a labeled 50 mL conical tube containing 20 mL wash medium A for decidual lymphocyte isolation.
Turn the placenta over so that the maternal surface (basal plate with cotyledons) is facing upwards.
Carefully cut thin pieces of approximately L = 2 x W = 1 x H = 0.5 cm³ size from the placenta basal plate using sterile scissors.
Avoid necrotic tissue and blood clots while cutting.
Gently spread out each piece of decidua basalis on your finger with the villi facing upwards.
Using scissors, carefully remove extra villi from the decidua basalis until a 2–3 mm thin membrane remains.
Collect approximately 15 mL decidua basalis tissue in a labeled 50 mL conical tube containing 30 mL 1× PBS.
Wash the tissues without centrifugation by adding sterile 1× PBS into each of the conical tubes.
Discard the supernatant after allowing the tissue to settle for approximately 1 minute.
Fill up the tubes with PBS and wash all tissues several times until the PBS is clear and there is no blood visible.
Cut the tissue into small (1–2 mm²) pieces inside the 50 mL falcon tube using scissors.
Wash the tissues without centrifugation by adding sterile 1× PBS into each of the conical tubes until the PBS is clear as described in step 5.
Let the tissues settle for 2 minutes to the bottom of the 50 mL conical tubes until no debris is visible in the PBS supernatant.
Measure the tissue volumes after settling.
Divide tissues between multiple conical tubes and create one tube containing 30 mL chorionic membrane and two tubes containing 7.5 mL decidua basalis tissue.
Divide decidua basalis tissue over two tubes.
Fill up all tubes with 1× PBS and centrifuge at 200 g for 1 min.
Carefully discard the supernatant from the tubes.
Transfer chorionic membrane tissue into a separate labeled 300 mL sterile bottle.
Transfer each 7.5 mL of decidua basalis tissue into separate labeled 300 mL sterile bottles.
Add 125 mL Tissue Digestion Enzyme Cocktail A to the bottle containing chorionic membranes and 100 mL to each of the two bottles containing decidua basalis.
Place the bottles containing decidua basalis tissue in a 37°C water bath and the bottle with chorionic tissue in a 39°C water bath for 15 min.
Agitate bottles every 3 min by hand for 30 s.
Let the tissue settle to the bottom of the bottles for approximately 1 minute.
Filter the supernatants through a metal dissociation sieve placed in a 15 cm petri dish.
Gently stir the solutions through the sieve (mesh size 40) with the back of a transfer pipette to strain the supernatant into the petri dish.
Add 10–30 mL Wash Medium B to the tissue and gently stir the solution through the sieve with the back of a transfer pipette to strain the supernatant into the petri dish.
Transfer undigested chorion and decidua basalis tissue into two separate 50 mL sterile conical tubes.
Fill the tubes with sterile ×1 PBS and centrifuge tissues at 650 g for 7 minutes.
Carefully discard the supernatant and transfer chorion and decidua basalis tissues into two labeled 300 mL bottles.
Repeat steps involving settling, filtering, washing, and separating tissue through digestion 2.
Filter all supernatants from the petri dishes through 100 μm cell strainers into 50 mL conical tubes.
Label the 50 mL conical tubes with the tissue type and the digestion number.
Maintain first digestion preparations separate from second digestion preparations for both chorionic membranes and decidua basalis tissue.
Centrifuge filtered supernatants at 650 g for 7 minutes.
Discard the supernatant.
Gently resuspend cell pellets with 5 mL Wash Medium B using a 2.5 mL bulb transfer pipette.
Combine cell pellets of the same tissue type and digestion number into one tube.
Create four tubes: i) chorion digest 1; ii) chorion digest 2; iii) basalis digest 1; iv) basalis digest 2.
Fill each tube with Wash Medium B to a total of 25 mL per tube.
Pipette 12.5 mL undiluted Ficoll into four 50 mL conical tubes (one for each digest).
Carefully layer 25 mL of resuspended cells over Ficoll without mixing the layers.
Centrifuge tubes at 800 g for 20 minutes (room temperature) without a brake.
Collect the cell layer at the interface in each tube using a sterile transfer pipette.
Transfer the collected layer into a separate 50 mL conical tube.
Fill up the tubes with Wash Medium B and centrifuge at 650 g for 7 minutes.
Carefully decant the supernatant.
Resuspend cell pellets containing EVT in 1 mL Wash Medium B.
Add anti-CD45-APC antibodies at a dilution of 1:50.
Add anti-EGRF1-AF488 antibodies at a dilution of 1:50.
Add anti-HLA-G-PE antibodies at a dilution of 1:100.
Incubate the mixture for 15 minutes at room temperature (20°C) in the dark.
Add 2 mL Wash Medium B and centrifuge cells at 650 g for 7 minutes.
Discard the supernatant.
Resuspend cell pellets carefully in 1.0 mL Wash Medium B.
Filter cells through a 40 μm cell strainer.
Transfer filtered cells to a 5 mL sterile FACS tube with cap.
Sort CD45-HLA-G+ EVT cells in Wash Medium B according to gating strategy using a 100 μm Nozzle at room temperature (20°C).
Centrifuge all cell fractions at 650 g for 7 min after cell sorting.
Discard the supernatant from the centrifuged samples.
Resuspend purified EVT at 1 × 10^6 cells/mL in Cell Culture Medium A or B as needed.
Maintain chorionic and basalis HLA-G+ EVT cells separately, though cells from first and second digestion can now be combined.
Seed 5 × 10^4 HLA-G+ EVT in 200 μL of Cell Culture Medium A on fibronectin-coated flat bottom 48 well culture plates.
Transfer cell culture plates to a humidified CO2 incubator at 37°C and let the cells adhere for 2 hours.
After the 2-hour incubation, HLA-G+ EVT are ready for experimentation including infection and/or co-culture with lymphocyte fractions.
Plate HLA-G+ EVT onto collagen-coated flat bottom culture wells to establish primary EVT-like cell lines.
Maintain optimal cell concentration for EVT growth and proliferation.
Seed 0.5–1 × 10^5 EVT cells in a 48 well cell culture plate with 200 μL Complete Cell Culture Medium B.
Seed 1–5 × 10^5 EVT cells in a 24 well cell culture plate with 1 mL Complete Cell Culture Medium B.
Seed 0.5–1 × 10^6 EVT cells in a 12 well cell culture plate with 1.5 mL Complete Cell Culture Medium B.
Seed 1–2 × 10^6 EVT cells in a 6 well cell culture plate with 2 mL Complete Cell Culture Medium B.
Transfer cell culture plates to humidified CO2 incubator at 37°C.
Replace the culture medium after 12–20 hours with fresh Complete Cell Culture Medium B.
Replace tissue medium with fresh Complete Cell Culture Medium B every two days.
Transfer EVT cultures to two same sized collagen pre-coated culture wells if they have 80%-90% confluency between day 3-7 after plating.
Transfer EVT to one same sized collagen pre-coated culture well if they have 40%-80% confluency at day 7 after plating.
Transfer EVT to a smaller sized collagen pre-coated culture well if they have 10%-40% confluency at day 7 after plating.
Remove cell culture medium from the wells in a tissue culture hood.
Add room temperature TrypLE Trypsin to the wells: 1.5 ml for a 6-well plate, 1 ml for a 12-well plate, 0.7 ml for a 24-well plate, or 0.1 ml for a 48-well plate.
Incubate at 37°C and 5% CO2 for 5 minutes.
Assess cells with a light microscope to confirm cell detachment from the culture plate.
If cells do not detach after another 3 minutes of incubation, repeat until EVT are detached.
Rinse wells with sterile Tissue Culture Medium A when cells are fully detached.
Centrifuge collected cells at 650 g for 7 minutes with a medium brake.
Discard the supernatant.
Gently resuspend the cell pellet in fresh Complete Cell Culture Medium B by flicking the tubes.
Transfer cells to appropriately sized, collagen-coated flat bottom culture wells.
Maintain optimal cell concentration with each transfer cycle.
Add freeze medium A and transfer cells to sterile 1.2 mL cryo tube after achieving desired confluency.
Slow freeze the cells in a cool cell at -80°C prior to transferring to liquid nitrogen for long term storage.
Trypsinize EVT-like cell lines as described in steps 44–46.
Add 2 × 10^5 cells to a 5 mL FACS tube in 100 μL basal medium.
Add cell surface antibodies for ITGA6, ECAD, EGFR1, HLA-G, HLA-E, HLA-C, PDL1, and B7-H3.
Incubate 20 minutes at room temperature in the dark.
Add 2 mL basal medium.
Centrifuge cells at 650 g for 7 minutes.
Discard supernatant.
Resuspend cell pellets in 0.5 mL basal medium carefully.
Acquire cells directly on a flow cytometer.
Isolate primary lymphocytes from the placenta according to Ikumi et al. 2023 protocols.
Seed 5 × 10^4 HLA-G+ EVT in 100 μL Cell Culture Medium A on fibronectin-coated flat bottom 48 well culture plates.
Seed 5 × 10^4 HLA-G+ EVT-like cell lines in 100 μL Complete Cell Culture Medium B on collagen-coated flat bottom 48 well culture plates.
Add 1 × 10^5 purified NK cells, T cells, or macrophages in 100 μL Cell Culture Medium C to the HLA-G+ EVT.
Mix Cell Culture Medium A and C in a 1:1 ratio for viability maintenance of EVT and leukocytes.
Add 2.5 ng/mL IL-15 to NK cultures for viability maintenance.
Add 50 U/mL IL-2 to T cell cultures for viability maintenance.
Include additional wells only containing HLA-G+ EVT or leukocyte fractions as negative controls.
Include additional wells with 1 μg/mL PMA and 1 μg/mL Ionomycin as positive controls for NK cells and T cells.
Include additional wells with 1 μg/mL anti-CD3/CD28 beads as positive controls for T cells.
Include additional wells with 100 ng/mL LPS as positive controls for macrophages.
